title: Associate Data Scientist II – Early Discovery Science
description:
About AbbVie
AbbVie's mission is to discover and deliver innovative medicines and solutions that solve serious health issues today and address the medical challenges of tomorrow. We strive to have a remarkable impact on people's lives across several key therapeutic areas including immunology, oncology and neuroscience - and products and services in our Allergan Aesthetics portfolio. For more information about AbbVie, please visit us at  www.abbvie.com . Follow @abbvie on  LinkedIn,   Facebook ,  Instagram ,  X  and  YouTube.
The Global Research, Informatics & Platform Solutions team within the Information Research (IR) Division partners with scientists and research organizations across AbbVie to unlock the value of scientific data. By enabling effective management, integration, and use of high-quality research data and delivering informatics platforms and decision-support capabilities, the team helps transform complex scientific information into actionable insights that accelerate discovery, strengthen scientific decision-making, and improve the efficiency and effectiveness of research and development. The role serves as a key bridge of expertise between laboratory scientists and technology teams and is responsible for defining, stewarding, and expanding our bioassay knowledge graph, translating scientific workflows into data solutions, and building data visualizations/AI-enabled solutions that accelerate drug discovery.
Responsibilities:
Perform assigned technical and analytic tasks using established methods and tools, select appropriate approaches for routine problems, document methods and results, and escalate novel or ambiguous issues.
Execute defined data extraction, transformation, and loading tasks using established tools and scripts.
Perform data cleaning and preprocessing on moderately complex datasets to prepare for analysis and modeling.
Conduct basic exploratory data analysis, including generating summary statistics and visualizations to identify trends and anomalies.
Assist in developing and validating simple statistical models and algorithms under guidance.
Write and run SQL queries (basic queries, table creation, views, and reporting) to extract, join, and prepare data for analysis and reporting.
Build dashboards, visualizations, and analyses in standard analytics platforms (e.g., Spotfire, Power BI, Tableau) using established templates and guidance.
Apply statistical and data mining techniques to scientific datasets, including bioassay data, and interprets results under guidance.
Support data flow and architecture work, including ETL pipelines, and helps troubleshoot workflows.
Partner with R&D scientists to understand data needs, and support scientific engagement and user training on delivered solutions.
Document data workflows, analysis procedures, and experimental results clearly and accurately for team review.
Deliver reliable outputs for assigned work and small projects, ensure acceptance criteria and compliance, documents methods, communicate progress and escalate high‑impact issues to project leads.
Required:
Bachelor's Degree and 2 years of experience; Master's Degree and 0 years of experience.
Background in a life sciences industry and data science.
Strong programming proficiency in Python required.
SQL skills (basic queries, table creation, views, and reporting)
Knowledge of statistical and data mining techniques
Working knowledge of data flow/architecture and ETL
Working knowledge of drug discovery and development process
Ability to work independently and within timelines in a fast-paced environment, managing multiple priorities effectively.
Addresses routine and some non-routine problems; communicates progress and results to supervisors.
Outstanding verbal, written and interpersonal skills for cross-functional collaboration, including proofreading, editing, and formatting technical documentation, and documenting and presenting technical solutions to non-technical stakeholders.
A self-motivated learner and thinker with a hands-on approach
Preferred:
Demonstrated technical proficiency in the pharmaceutical industry highly preferred.
Familiarity with data visualization and pipelining tools such as Spotfire, Power BI, Tableau, or similar
Working knowledge of bioassay analysis.
Familiarity with GitHub or other version control tools.

title: Associate Director, Enterprise Forecasting Platform Product Owner
description:
About AbbVie
AbbVie's mission is to discover and deliver innovative medicines and solutions that solve serious health issues today and address the medical challenges of tomorrow. We strive to have a remarkable impact on people's lives across several key therapeutic areas including immunology, oncology and neuroscience - and products and services in our Allergan Aesthetics portfolio. For more information about AbbVie, please visit us at  www.abbvie.com . Follow @abbvie on  LinkedIn,   Facebook ,  Instagram ,  X  and  YouTube.
Purpose:
AbbVie’s Global Forecasting Center of Excellence (COE) sustains and advances the organization’s volume forecasting capabilities established under Finance Transformation Forecasting Excellence. The COE defines forecasting standards, governs best practices, oversees deployment of enabling technologies, executes centralized forecasting functions on behalf of the organization, and builds forecasting competencies across AbbVie’s US, International, and Allergan Aesthetics commercial organizations.
The COE’s Operations & Insights pillar is the operational and analytical engine that powers enterprise forecasting at scale, encompassing AI and statistical modeling and governance, forecasting platform management, and centralized analytics. The Enterprise Forecasting Platform team is a key component of the COE and is responsible for the business ownership, operation, adoption, and continued evolution of AbbVie’s enterprise forecasting platform.
Position Overview
The Associate Director, Enterprise Forecasting Platform Product Owner is accountable for the business ownership, strategy, ongoing management, and evolution of AbbVie’s enterprise forecasting platform. The role owns the product vision and roadmap, prioritizes capabilities and enhancements, drives adoption and effective utilization, oversees platform economics, and ensures the product continues to meet evolving enterprise forecasting needs.
This role serves as a key business owner of the relationship with the platform vendor. It establishes platform performance expectations, manages service levels and commitments, oversees adoption and utilization measures, and ensures AbbVie realizes appropriate value from its investment.
The Product Owner works closely with forecasters, Finance leadership, Forecasting COE teams, Business Technology Solutions (BTS), data and analytics partners, Procurement, and the platform vendor to translate business needs into platform priorities and deliver an effective foundation for enterprise forecasting processes.
Core Job Responsibilities:
Enterprise Product Ownership & Strategy
Serve as the business product owner for AbbVie’s enterprise forecasting platform, accountable for overall business value, usability, adoption, and continued evolution.
Define and maintain the product vision, strategy, and multi-year roadmap in alignment with Global Forecasting COE priorities and enterprise business needs.
Develop and manage strategic and tactical roadmaps that translate forecasting needs into sequenced platform capabilities and enhancements.
Own business prioritization of platform features, functionality, integrations, and enhancements.
Maintain and prioritize the business product backlog in partnership with BTS, the vendor, the COE, Finance, and forecasting stakeholders.
Establish clear prioritization criteria based on enterprise value, user impact, cost, risk, implementation complexity, and operational readiness.
Evaluate opportunities to expand or improve platform capabilities as forecasting processes, analytical methods, data availability, and technologies evolve.
Vendor & Commercial Management
Own the strategic business relationship with the enterprise forecasting platform vendor and serve as the primary point of accountability for vendor performance.
Define, monitor, and enforce vendor success measures and service-level agreements (SLAs).
Establish regular vendor governance and performance reporting covering enhancements, defects, service levels, contractual commitments, open issues, risks, and remediation plans.
Hold the vendor accountable for delivery against agreed priorities, timelines, service expectations, and contractual obligations.
Partner with Procurement, BTS, Finance, Legal, and other functions on contract renewals, commercial discussions, and vendor evaluations.
Monitor platform consumption and contractual usage where applicable and identify potential cost, capacity, or service implications.
Maintain visibility into total product cost and value, including vendor fees and associated investments required to operate and enhance the platform.
Assess whether the vendor roadmap and capabilities remain aligned with AbbVie’s evolving forecasting needs.
Platform Implementation, Operations & Continuous Improvement
Oversee the business implementation of platform releases, enhancements, and new capabilities, ensuring solutions meet agreed requirements and compliance expectations.
Partner with BTS and the vendor to translate forecasting needs into clear product requirements, acceptance criteria, and implementation priorities.
Establish processes for intake, triage, prioritization, escalation, and resolution of platform issues and enhancement requests.
Monitor platform performance and user experience, identifying recurring friction points and opportunities to simplify or improve forecasting workflows.
Ensure platform changes consider impacts to upstream data, forecasting processes, analytical outputs, downstream planning activities, and end users.
Maintain product documentation, decision history, requirements, roadmap materials, operational procedures, and key institutional knowledge.
Drive continuous product improvement.
Adoption & Capability Building
Partner with COE and the Forecast Excellence team to champion the forecasting platform across the organization, create a clear understanding of its value and appropriate use, and identify and address barriers to adoption.
Develop a structured approach for measuring platform adoption, utilization, user experience, and business value.
Build feedback mechanisms that allow forecasters and Finance stakeholders to influence product priorities while maintaining disciplined enterprise governance.
Translate platform capabilities into clear, practical implications for forecasting teams.
Stakeholder Management & Governance
Act as the primary business interface among forecasting users, COE leadership, Finance leadership, BTS, data and analytics teams, Procurement, and the platform vendor.
Capture and synthesize requirements from brands, geographies, and forecasting teams into enterprise-level priorities.
Proactively manage expectations regarding roadmap priorities, delivery timing, platform limitations, dependencies, and tradeoffs.
Establish transparent governance for major product decisions and investment priorities.
Regularly communicate the product roadmap, progress, risks, adoption, issues, vendor performance, and business value to COE and Finance leadership.
Co-Lead workshops and decision forums (in partnership with Standards and Training) needed to align stakeholders around product choices and future capabilities.
Escalate material platform or vendor risks and drive them through resolution.
Financial & Resource Management
Develop and manage the business case and budget associated with the enterprise forecasting platform.
Maintain transparency into platform costs, vendor spend, enhancement investments, and required resources.
Evaluate the costs, expected benefits, and organizational implications of significant platform enhancements and investments.
Partner with Finance, BTS, Procurement, and COE leadership to inform investment and resource-allocation decisions.
Identify opportunities to improve the economic efficiency of the platform while protecting critical enterprise forecasting capabilities.
Team / People Leadership
Lead and guide team members supporting forecasting platform product management, operations, analytics, and user support as the operating model evolves.
Own prioritization and work planning for the team, ensuring resources are allocated to the highest-value platform needs.
Provide regular feedback, coaching, and career-development support to team members.
Build strong product-management capability within the Operations & Insights organization.
Create a culture of user orientation, accountability, transparency, and continuous improvement.
Reporting
Reports to: Director, Forecasting Operations & Insights
Direct reports: Team members supporting enterprise forecasting platform product management, operations, analytics, and user support, with size determined by the evolving operating model.
ualifications
Required:
Bachelor’s degree in Business, Finance, Analytics, Information Technology, Data Science, Engineering, or a related field; advanced degree preferred.
10+ years of progressive experience in product management, platform ownership, forecasting, analytics, technology-enabled business transformation, or related roles.
Demonstrated experience owning or managing a complex enterprise technology product or platform through implementation, adoption, optimization, and ongoing evolution.
Demonstrated ability to develop product strategies and roadmaps and translate business needs into prioritized technology capabilities and requirements.
Experience managing external technology or platform vendors, including performance, delivery commitments, issue escalation, and commercial considerations.
Strong understanding of enterprise data, analytics, technology, and the dependencies required to operationalize technology-enabled business processes.
Demonstrated ability to work effectively with business, data, analytics, and technology teams and translate between technical and non-technical stakeholders.
Proven ability to lead complex, matrixed initiatives involving multiple stakeholder groups and competing priorities.
Strong executive communication and stakeholder-management skills, including experience communicating product decisions, tradeoffs, risks, and recommendations to senior leaders.
Ability to operate effectively under ambiguity, make disciplined prioritization decisions, and manage multiple concurrent priorities.
Preferred:
Experience in the pharmaceutical, biotech, life sciences, or another complex global commercial organization.
Experience with commercial forecasting, financial planning, analytics, or decision-support platforms.
Familiarity with pharmaceutical volume forecasting and planning cycles such as LBE, Plan, and LRP.
Experience managing enterprise software-as-a-service platforms and vendor relationships.
Experience establishing product governance, adoption metrics, service expectations, and product-performance reporting.
Experience working with forecasting or planning technologies and their supporting data ecosystems.
Familiarity with AI, machine learning, and statistical forecasting capabilities and how they integrate into enterprise forecasting workflows.
Experience managing platform budgets, contracts, business cases, and technology investment decisions.

title: Sr Scientist or Scientist, Systems Immunology
description:
About AbbVie

AbbVie Immunology is expanding its discovery Systems Immunology team in Cambridge, Massachusetts. The team is focused on identifying new targets for the treatment of autoimmune and chronic inflammatory diseases through computational analysis of human disease tissue-derived datasets and validating targets using humanized experimental approaches.
We are seeking a highly motivated and skilled individual to join our team as a Computational Immunology Scientist. The successful candidate will develop and implement computational approaches to understand disease biology and drug responses using high-throughput molecular profiling data. This role will involve integrating single-cell RNA-seq, scATAC-seq, TCR/BCR repertoire, bulk RNA-seq, and Olink proteomics data to characterize disease-associated cell states, investigate gene regulatory networks, and identify therapeutic opportunities.
The scientist will work in a multidisciplinary team analyzing multiomics datasets to derive insights into immunological diseases and identify novel therapeutic targets relevant to patient cohorts and AbbVie pipeline drugs. The candidate will also contribute to scientific conference presentations, peer-reviewed publications of translational findings, new drug applications, and regulatory filings. If you are passionate about translating complex biological data into actionable insights and advancing personalized medicine, we encourage you to apply.
This position will be based in Cambridge, Massachusetts, and requires passion, attention to detail, prior hands-on experience, and teamwork.
Key Responsibilities:
Analyze scRNA-seq, and CITE-seq, datasets, including quality control, integration, clustering, and cell-type and cell-state annotation.
Integrate patient cohorts with reference atlases and perform differential expression, abundance, and pathway analyses, accounting for donor variation and study design.
Analyze scATAC-seq data to identify differential accessibility, transcription factor motifs, and candidate regulatory programs; integrate accessibility with gene expression to infer peak-to-gene relationships.
Analyze TCR/BCR repertoires, including clonotype assignment, clonal expansion, diversity, V(D)J usage, and sharing across tissues or time points; link clonotypes to matched single-cell profiles.
Analyze bulk RNA-seq and Olink proteomics data and integrate multiomics findings to support target prioritization and biomarker hypotheses; maintain documented, version-controlled workflows and evaluate methods using cloud or high-performance computing.
Collaborate with internal and external scientists to prioritize hypotheses for validation, communicate findings and limitations, and contribute to presentations and publications.
BS, MS, or PhD in computational biology, bioinformatics, genomics, biostatistics, computer science, or a related quantitative field with typically 5-12 years (BS), 2-10 years (MS), or 0-4 years (PhD) of relevant experience.
Hands-on scRNA-seq analysis experience or experience with scATAC-seq or TCR/BCR analysis, with interest in developing expertise across both.
Proficiency in Python and/or R and experience working in Linux-based computing environments.
Experience with commonly used bioinformatics tools and frameworks such as Scanpy, AnnData, Cell Ranger, scvi-tools, DESeq2, GSEA, WGCNA, or related methods.
Working knowledge of statistical analysis, multiple-testing correction, batch effects, and biological replication in high-dimensional datasets.
Ability to translate biological questions into analyses, interpret and communicate results critically, collaborate effectively, and manage multiple priorities with attention to detail.
Demonstrated ability to work collaboratively, manage multiple priorities, and deliver high-quality analyses with attention to detail.
Preferred Qualifications:
Experience analyzing Olink or other high-plex proteomics datasets.
Experience with CITE-seq, ATAC-seq, spatial transcriptomics, or integrative multi-omics analysis.
Experience building or benchmarking machine-learning models, including convolutional neural networks, autoencoders, generative models, transfer learning, or foundation models.
Experience with cloud or high-performance computing, including AWS and/or SLURM.
Understanding of immunology and inflammatory disease biology; experience supporting target discovery with experimental teams and communicating research through presentations, publications, or reports.
Evidence of scientific communication through presentations, posters, publications, technical reports, or related research contributions.

title: Operations Program Manager, Electronics Supply Chain, Amazon Leo
description:
Are you passionate about electronics manufacturing and ready to play a key role in bringing satellite hardware to life? Amazon Leo is building a low Earth orbit satellite broadband network designed to deliver fast, reliable internet to customers and communities around the world. As the team develops new products and scales production, we are looking for a collaborative, curious Operations Program Manager to join the Electronic Supply Chain team and drive Printed Circuit Board Assembly (PCBA) manufacturing operations with our contract manufacturers.
In this role, you will own the end-to-end production lifecycle for assigned PCBAs, working closely with contract manufacturers to ensure quality and on-time delivery. You will use tools such as SAP and generative AI alongside your electronics manufacturing expertise to identify process improvements, resolve production blockers, and support the team through a period of exciting growth. This is a great opportunity for someone who thrives in a fast-paced environment and wants to build their career while contributing to a product with global impact.
Key job responsibilities
- Manage contract manufacturers' end-to-end PCBA production processes, coordinating production planning and execution aligned with cross-functional priorities
- Lead technical deep dives to identify root causes of manufacturing blockers and implement corrective actions that keep builds on schedule
- Drive continuous improvement initiatives across supplier operations, optimizing capacity, quality, and production efficiency using data analysis and structured problem-solving
- Collaborate with engineering, quality, and supply chain teams to support new product introductions and balance development needs with ongoing production commitments
- Present production status updates and improvement proposals to leadership, communicating requirements clearly and negotiating priorities across stakeholders
A day in the life
You will start your morning reviewing delivery schedules, work-in-progress status, and production metrics across your assigned contract manufacturers. Daily stand-ups with cross-functional partners help you prioritize blockers and align on paths to resolution. From there, you might analyze supplier performance data to pinpoint bottlenecks, join technical reviews with engineering teams to evaluate new design requirements, or coordinate with quality on corrective actions. Some weeks you will travel to supplier sites for hands-on problem-solving and capacity planning. Throughout it all, you will balance tactical execution with longer-term thinking to keep production on track as the team scales.
About the team
The Electronic Supply Chain team within Amazon Leo is responsible for ensuring satellite PCBA production meets the quality and pace required to support our broadband network. We work closely with contract manufacturers, engineering, and quality teams to deliver reliable hardware on schedule. As the team grows and new products come online, we are investing in our people just as much as our processes. You can expect increasing autonomy, broader project scope, and clear pathways to take on larger responsibilities over time. We value mentorship, career development, and a collaborative environment where everyone contributes to our shared mission of connecting communities worldwide.
Basic qualifications: - 3+ years of technical product or program management experience
- 3+ years of project management disciplines including scope, schedule, budget, quality, along with risk and critical path management experience
- Experience managing programs across cross functional teams, building processes and coordinating release schedules
Preferred qualifications: - 3+ years of working directly with engineering teams experience
- 3+ years of working within electronics supply chain teams and/or within a printed circuit board assembly (PCBA) manufacturing environment.

title: Senior Product Manager, Technical, Supply Tech - Advertising
description:
Amazon Ads is one of the fastest-growing advertising businesses in the world, connecting brands with hundreds of millions of customers across shopping, streaming, gaming, audio and the open web. Behind every ad that runs on Prime Video, Twitch, IMDb and thousands of external publisher apps and sites is a decisioning platform built by Amazon Ads Supply Tech.
That platform makes X trillion ad decisions every day. It supports $XB+ in annual publisher revenue across XX+ Amazon-owned publishers and X,000+ external publishers in streaming TV, audio, display, mobile and podcasts. In real time and at massive scale, it decides which inventory qualifies for which buyers, how publisher commitments to advertisers are met, which ad wins among competing candidates, and how pricing adjusts to maximize yield. Each of these decisions balances the interests of advertisers, publishers, viewers and Amazon. At this scale, a fraction-of-a-percent improvement is worth $X millions and reaches X million customers.
We are looking for a Senior Product Manager – Technical to own the strategy for a key area of this platform. You will find the most important customer problems, work backwards to a clear strategy, and deliver with world-class engineers and applied scientists. Then you will operate and grow what you have launched. Your work will directly shape three of Amazon Ads’ biggest priorities: growing Amazon-owned and third-party supply, enabling full-funnel advertising, and building agentic, AI-driven workflows for publishers and advertisers.
You will join a team of builders, product leaders and scientists who set high standards, care deeply about customers, and invest in each other’s growth. If you want to work on hard, large-scale problems with excellent colleagues, and see your decisions move a multi-billion-dollar business, this role is for you.
Key job responsibilities
• Own the strategy and roadmap for a specific area of the ad decisioning platform.
• Work backwards from customers. Talk with publishers, advertisers and internal partners to find their biggest problems, then define solutions that improve outcomes for everyone in the marketplace.
• Partner deeply with Applied Science to turn auction, pricing, forecasting and ML models into products that ship. Define success metrics, design experiments and use the results to make decisions.
• Partner with Engineering on architecture, APIs and system tradeoffs for headless, low-latency, high-availability services that run at X trillion decisions a day.
• Execute end to end. Write PRFAQs and requirements, prioritize ruthlessly, drive launches across multiple teams and marketplaces, then operate and improve the product after launch.
• Balance competing objectives across publisher yield, advertiser performance, viewer experience and long-term business health. Make clear, data-driven tradeoffs and explain them crisply.
• Own the business results of your area: set goals, track inputs and outputs, report progress in business reviews, and raise the bar on how the team measures impact.
• Identify and drive AI-native opportunities, including agentic workflows that make the platform easier to use for publishers and advertisers and help it make better decisions.
A day in the life
Your day might start in a working session with applied scientists. Together you would review experiment results for a new pricing model that lifts publisher yield by X% without hurting the viewer experience, and decide whether it is ready to scale. Next, you would join a design review with senior engineers to work through how a new inventory qualification capability will serve X billion requests with no added latency.
At midday you might meet a streaming TV publisher partner to understand why a commitment they made to a major advertiser is under-delivering, and turn that conversation into a problem statement your team can solve. In the afternoon you would refine a PRFAQ for next year’s strategy and align with demand-side and sales leaders on a worldwide launch plan. Before you sign off, you would check your area’s operational and business metrics and flag a trend for the team to dig into tomorrow.
Throughout the day you will work with smart, driven colleagues who challenge your thinking, back your decisions and help you grow. You will go home knowing your work affected a business of global scale.

Ads Decisioning team is a group of product managers and applied scientists building the decisioning layer behind Amazon's publisher business. We serve Amazon-owned publishers such as Prime Video, Twitch and IMDb, along with thousands of external publishers across streaming TV, audio and display. Our systems decide, in milliseconds, which inventory qualifies for which buyers, how commitments are delivered, which ad wins and at what price, balancing advertisers, publishers, viewers and Amazon. We obsess over customers, hold a high bar for rigor and operational excellence, and invest in each other's growth. Come do the best work of your career.

title: Sr Product Manager, OTS Delivery Software Engineering (DSE)
description:
Every Amazon package that ships, every grocery order that is fulfilled, and every associate who needs IT help depends on technology our teams keep running. Amazon's OpsTech Solutions (OTS) is the IT operations and infrastructure organization for all of Amazon Worldwide Operations, including Worldwide Grocery Stores (WWGS), delivering reliable technology to more than one million associates and operators across every geography. OTS is transforming from reactive support to proactive, prescriptive, AI-powered service delivery, and ServiceNow is the platform where that work happens.
What this role is: You will own the product experience for how work moves between ServiceNow and other ticketing platforms (e.g. SIM-T) and the integration strategy that lets OTS scale as more partner teams and platforms connect. Cross-organization resolver groups depend on SIM-T, so the connection to ServiceNow has to work reliably. Better integration gives our customers the information they need when they need it, wherever they are. You will decide what information synchronizes, how paging and engagement work, and how the integration grows as new partner teams are added.
Our team is organized around three questions that apply to every persona we serve: How does someone ask for help? How does the organization receive and organize that work? How does the work get resolved? This role sits where the answers meet other organizations. OTS depends on these integrations to send work items to teams outside the OTS organization. Your peers own the requester front door (OneSupportHub and Virtual Agent), the Incident Management Platform (ITSM), Service Desk Workforce Optimization, and AI resolution intelligence (OTS Assist and PathFinder). The decisions you make determine whether work reaches the right team with the right context, and whether those peers' products work as intended once work leaves ServiceNow.
The opportunity is to turn a fragile integration into a well-governed product. You will define the fields and information that synchronize between platforms, the paging and engagement models, the experience for managing CTI to category/subcategory mapping, and the governance for how catalog item flows synchronize. You will also define the integration strategy as the business scales. As more partner teams and platforms need to send work to OTS or receive work from it, you will set the principles, standards, and requirements for how those integrations are built, onboarded, and governed, and you will keep OTS's needs represented as that work evolves. The SIM-T work gives you a strong foundation, because the lessons from that integration become the pattern for every new connection. Your customers are Service Desk fulfillers, Field IT technicians and managers, and the partner teams that send and receive OTS work.
Key Highlights
• Own the product experience for ServiceNow integration, from paging and escalation to information synchronization.
• Define the data, paging, and engagement models that govern work sent to teams outside OTS.
• Own the experience for CTI to category/subcategory mapping and the governance of catalog item flow synchronization.
• Define the integration strategy that lets OTS scale as the business grows, and partner with external teams.
• Work at the center of a product team whose adjacent products (intake, ITSM, routing, workforce optimization, AI resolution) all depend on work moving reliably between systems.

- Define and own the product vision and roadmap for ServiceNow integration with SIM-T and other ticketing platforms, and prioritize improvements against the gaps customers experience.
- Define which fields and lifecycle events synchronize between platforms, including status, severity, type conversion, transfers, and escalation, and the rules for resolving conflicts.

- Define the UI/UX for managing CTI to category/subcategory mapping, working with UX and engineering partners.
- Establish governance for catalog item flow synchronization, including how new catalog items and partner teams are onboarded.
- Act as the voice of the customer for Service Desk, Field IT, and partner teams, using shadowing, feedback, and operational data to translate real workflow friction into prioritized requirements.
- Define and maintain OTS's integration strategy and standards for partner platforms and teams, including what data and context pass between systems and how new integrations are onboarded, in partnership with partner teams.
- Set up an intake and prioritization process for new integration requests, so OTS can decide consistently what to accept, defer, or decline.
- Contribute to annual planning mechanisms (OP1/OP2) with clear, well-reasoned investment proposals, and maintain mechanisms to continuously capture voice of the customer.
A day in the life
Your day moves between the floor and the roadmap. You might start by reviewing a handful of tickets that failed to sync, tracing where information was lost and which rule needs to change. Midday, you meet with a partner platform team to decide which integration requirements are in scope for the next phase and how they fit the broader integration strategy. In the afternoon, you work with UX and engineering on a mapping workflow for CTI to category/subcategory, meet with a partner team that wants to start sending work to OTS, and draft a requirements document or an OP2 investment proposal for senior review.

The ServiceNow Product Management team builds the products that are the backbone of OTS operations. Amazon employees, Service Desk agents, and Field IT technicians rely on these ServiceNow experiences to complete their work every day. The team is a group of Product Managers, each owning one clear product space so they can go deep instead of switching between unrelated problems, supported by a dedicated UX designer. Your engineering counterparts sit within the same larger organization, and your primary stakeholders are the Service Desk and Field IT organizations and the partner teams outside OTS that send and receive work.

title: Sr. Research Scientist , WW Sustainability
description:
Join the Worldwide Sustainability (WWS) organization where we capitalize on our size, scale, and inventive culture to build a more resilient and sustainable company. WWS manages our social and environmental impacts globally, driving solutions that enable our customers, businesses, and the world around us to become more sustainable.
Sustainability Science and Innovation is a multi-disciplinary team within the WW Sustainability organization that combines science, analytics, economics, statistics, machine learning, product development, and engineering expertise to identify, evaluate and/or develop new science, technologies, and innovations that aim to address long-term sustainability challenges.
We are seeking an organic chemist with deep, hands-on synthesis expertise to anchor the experimental core of our materials chemistry program. This role brings materials into the real world from an in silico discovery pipeline — through an automated, high-throughput lab — designing and executing the chemical synthesis and characterization that turn computational predictions and hypotheses into physical materials with measured properties. You will be the senior hands-on scientist and technical lead for chemical synthesis and experimental characterization, setting the experimental standard for the lab and partnering closely with our computational scientists and the autonomous-lab team to tighten the design–make–test–analyze loop.
This is a bench-first, individual-contributor role. The people who do best here are hands-on experimentalists who are energized by hard synthesis problems, hold themselves to rigorous experimental and safety standards, and want to raise the craft of everyone around them.
Key job responsibilities
Design scalable synthesis methods and execute high-throughput and automated experimentation to accelerate synthesis and screening.
Characterize materials properties and performance, and benchmark experimental results against computational predictions.
Establish and maintain rigorous experimental methods, SOPs, and data-quality standards, keeping reproducible records suitable for independent review.
Partner with computational scientists and automation engineers to tighten the design–make–test–analyze loop, feeding experimental results back to refine candidate selection.
A day in the life
You'll spend your day where ideas meet physical validation — at the bench and on the instruments — as we build our autonomous lab and AI-driven materials discovery platform spanning the full arc from computational discovery to real-world deployment. A typical day might start by designing a set of synthesis experiments, kicking off a high-throughput run, and prepping samples for characterization. By mid-day you're interpreting experimental data, benchmarking what you measured against the computational predictions, and deciding which candidates move forward. You'll close the loop with your computational and automation partners — feeding results back to sharpen the next round — and carve out time to document methods and findings so the work holds up to independent review.
About the team
Diverse Experiences:
World Wide Sustainability (WWS) values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. title: Sr. TPM, Live Sports, Prime Video Sports & Linear Operations
description:
Millions of fans stream live sports and events on Prime Video, from the Thursday Night Football, NBA Playoffs, NASCAR, MLB, MLS, and The Emmy's, to international soccer, cricket, and tennis. When a game is on, there is no second chance: if fans can't get into the stream or it cuts out at a key moment, we lose their trust. We're looking for a Senior Technical Program Manager to lead the programs that keep our live events available and high quality for every fan, on every device, every time. Our live event lineup grows by double digits every year, so our systems, processes and standards need to scale just as fast to keep every event reliable for fans.
You'll own how we define, measure and improve the live event experience across our own broadcasts and the ones we deliver with partners. You'll work with engineering, product, operations and partner teams to find the weak spots in our systems before game day, drive fixes that prevent repeat issues, and make sure our metrics reflect what fans actually experience. This role suits someone who is technically curious, comfortable with ambiguity, and motivated by work that customers notice right away.
Key job responsibilities
- Own the live event availability goal from start to finish: define what "available" means for fans, set targets, and report progress to senior leadership.
- Lead cross-team programs that close gaps in how we detect and measure issues during live event. Examples include fans who can't start a stream, get kicked out early or join late.
- Drive post-incident reviews and make sure the resulting fixes are actually delivered, so the same problem doesn't happen twice.
- Set and roll out operational standards for content partners, including pre-event checks, communication during major events and change deadlines, and help partners meet them.
- Partner with engineering on readiness for high-profile events: testing, monitoring, release controls and backup plans.
- Build clear reporting and dashboards that give leaders an honest view of quality and risk.
- Write clear narratives and plans that align teams and leaders on priorities, trade-offs and investments.
- Find recurring problems in incident data and turn them into long-term programs rather than one-off fixes.
A day in the life
Your morning might start with a review of last night's NBA doubleheader: what went well, what fans experienced, and whether anything needs a deeper look. Next you could meet with engineering leads about a gap in monitoring, then join a call with a content partner to walk through pre-event requirements ahead of a cricket tournament or a NASCAR weekend. In the afternoon you might refine a proposal for next year's quality goals or prepare a leadership update. On Thursday Night Football nights or during a live awards show, you'll work closely with operations and engineering teams to make sure everyone is ready, and you'll help lead the response if something goes wrong. No two days are the same. The live calendar runs from fall football to spring playoffs to summer racing and keeps the pace energizing, and your work shows up directly in the fan experience.

title: US-Lead
description:
Apple Retail is where the best of Apple comes together. We bring our expertise to help people do what they love, delivering an only-at-Apple experience. We believe inclusion is a shared responsibility and we work together to foster a culture where everyone belongs and is inspired to do their best work.
As a Lead, you embody a whole-store mindset and are integral to supporting the Store Leadership team, playing a critical role in facilitating meaningful experiences for both customers and team members. You inform and energize our teams to do their best work and contribute to operational excellence. You actively connect with team members, making sure everyone is equipped with the support, tools, and resources they need to deliver exceptional customer interactions.
A Lead works alongside the leadership team to ensure operational readiness, with a focus on enabling the sales team. You spend the majority of your time with the team and customers, identifying ownership opportunities and supporting team members across the whole store.
Lead, act as a role model, mentor, and encourage customer engagement.
Use Apple product and services expertise to drive customer engagement and sales, while building customer loyalty.
Organize people and the sales floor workflow, including managing relevant communication to team members and leadership to optimize the customer experience.
Make sure that sales strategy is effectively communicated to the team in a timely manner and executed in partnership with the leadership team.
Energize, inform, and align team members on store performance goals, priorities, and communication.
Attend to time-sensitive team member feedback, questions, and concerns, and escalate issues to Store Leadership as appropriate.
Address operational needs of the store, such as opening and closing procedures, cash management, and overrides.
Perform other tasks as needed, including but not limited to providing customer service and support in other areas of the store.
Contribute to an inclusive environment by respecting each other’s differences and having the curiosity to learn.
Demonstrate Apple’s values of inclusion and diversity in daily activities.
Minimum qualifications: You should:
Be available to work a schedule based on business needs that may include nights, weekends, and public holidays in the retail store, and reliably attend work as scheduled, in line with local laws and subject to any approved accommodations.
Have experience in retail or sales, or related work experience.
Have experience mentoring or leading others personally or professionally.
Preferred qualifications: You can:
Motivate others to achieve performance goals by fostering open dialog, collaboration, and recognition.
Resolve conflict and settle differences in productive ways.
Work in a fast-paced environment and make timely decisions using analytics, experience, and judgment.
Demonstrate excellent attention to detail and organization skills.
Work autonomously and be willing to take initiative without close supervision.
Drive results both individually and through enabling others by leading and collaborating.
Allocate resources and adjust processes to provide an exceptional customer experience.
Communicate effectively and tailor your communication style to different audiences.

title: Deployment Engineer (Logistics & Distribution)
description:
ABOUT BASE

Base is America’s next-generation power company. We’re rebuilding the foundation of modern civilization–electricity–by deploying a vast network of distributed batteries that is transforming today’s fragile, centralized grid into a resilient and abundant system. We are engineers, operators, and creatives solving some of the most complex, interdisciplinary challenges of our time.




ABOUT THE ROLE

Base is launching new products, new deployment models, and new facilities in rapid succession. As we scale from early-stage operations to a high-throughput deployment engine, we need someone who can engineer the processes that hold it all together. We are hiring a Deployments Engineer to own the end-to-end process architecture for our warehousing and logistics function—creating the playbooks, systems, and workflows that will allow us to replicate successful operations across any new market or product.

This is a process engineering role with a strong operational execution component. You will be embedded with the warehouse and manufacturing teams, solving hard problems with a first-principles mindset and leaving behind scalable, documented systems.

 

What You’ll Do

 - Create and maintain a comprehensive, living playbook with all processes, tasks, SOPs, and a master timeline to enable repeatable (“copy + paste”) warehouse standups.

 - Document all current-state workflows and identify gaps or inconsistencies that introduce risk or inefficiency.

 - Maintain version control and communicate playbook updates to relevant stakeholders as processes evolve.

 - Lead process engineering efforts to support pivots and fulfillment of new projects and products as they arise.

 - Conduct root cause analysis on operational mistakes and implement systemic fixes.

 - Design physical and digital workflow improvements to reduce cycle times, errors, and operational costs.

 - Partner with Software teams to translate process requirements into tooling features or automations and coordinate their implementation.

 - Serve as the operational liaison between manufacturing and deployment, ensuring handoff processes are well-defined and executed.



What You’ll Bring

 - 3–6 years of experience in process engineering, industrial engineering, operations engineering, or a closely related field.

 - Demonstrated ability to design, document, and implement scalable operational processes in a physical or hybrid (physical + digital) environment.

 - Experience collaborating with manufacturing, warehouse, or supply chain teams in a fast-paced, high-growth environment.

 - Strong technical foundation—able to translate operational workflows into systems requirements and work credibly alongside software teams.

 - Excellent written communication skills; able to produce clear, concise SOPs and process documentation that others can execute independently.

 - First-principles thinking and comfort challenging the status quo with data and structured reasoning.

 - Experience with ERP or WMS platforms is strongly preferred.



About the Team

The Deployments Warehousing & Logistics team is responsible for the physical infrastructure that makes Base installs possible—managing warehouse locations, orchestrating inter-warehouse transfers, running final-mile logistics, and ensuring inventory accuracy across our internal systems. We solve the difficult, high impact problems that determine whether crews show up to job sites ready to work. Joining this team means owning processes that directly impact Base’s ability to scale and deliver on its mission.



Please note: Base is a startup, which means priorities shift and evolve quickly. Your role may expand or change based on the needs of the business at any given time, so the responsibilities listed may not be exhaustive.




OUR VALUES

 - First Principles Thinking: Question assumptions. Principles > rules.

 - Operate at Base Pace: Focus on what matters, act quickly, and learn by doing.

 - Give & Get Feedback: Be direct, be humble, and maintain a growth mindset.

 - Everyone’s an Owner: Follow through on commitments and own results.

 - Strong Opinions, Loosely Held: Drive clarity and make calls with imperfect information.

 - Committed to the Mission: Rebuilding the grid is a big challenge. We work hard because we care deeply about the impact we’re creating. We work in-person. It’s not a 9-to-5. We are all-in.

 - Fun & Optimism Coexist with Grit: Collaboration and celebration coincide with the intensity of building real things.
   
   


DO THE BEST WORK OF YOUR LIFE AT BASE.

As a new team member in our North American Operations group, you'll begin by immersing yourself in our company culture and mastering world-class operations. Work and communicate cross-functionally within Flexport
Be a part of the frontline groups ensuring the highest standard of Flexport quality: shipments move on time and exceptions are handled appropriately.
Use metrics to spot opportunities to improve and deliver great performance in your role.

Consistently follow Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) to ensure that your work satisfies internal Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) and Service-Level Agreements (SLAs) in line with productivity goals.
You should have:
Bachelor's/Associate's degree OR 1+ year of relevant experience preferred. New graduates are encouraged to apply!
Team-centric mindset: obsessed with team outcomes, doing what it takes to deliver the team’s and their client’s expectations.
Strong written and verbal communication skills.
Strong attention to detail in a high-energy, fast-paced environment.
Proficient in Google Suite/Microsoft Suite (Sheets/Excel).
Fluency in English, both written and verbal.
A "compliance first" attitude to keep our regulators happy and enthusiastic about Flexport since we operate in a heavily regulated industry.

description:
Are you ready to build America’s energy future? Form Energy is an American manufacturing and energy technology company. We’re revolutionizing energy storage with cost-effective, multi-day technology designed to keep the electric grid secure and reliable, even during extended periods of stress. By strengthening the electric system and reimagining what’s possible, we’re giving clean energy a whole new form! 



In recent years, Form Energy has earned a number of accolades, including being named by TIME as a “Best Invention”, MIT Technology Review as a “Top Climate Tech Company To Watch”, and Fast Company as “One of the Next Big Things In Tech”. We are making rapid progress on our mission of delivering energy storage for a better world, and our team is growing just as rapidly to meet demand. We have signed contracts with leading electric utilities across the United States and production of our iron-air batteries is underway at our first high-volume manufacturing facility in West Virginia. 



Working for Form Energy is more than just a job, it’s a chance to be part of something extraordinary. And now - right as we significantly scale up battery manufacturing -  might be the most exciting moment in the company’s history to join. We are assembling a team of highly talented and driven individuals across the country. Driven by our core values of humanity, excellence, and creativity, our team is determined to deliver on our mission and transform the energy landscape for the better.



Feeling energized to make a meaningful impact on the world? Then keep reading - you’ve come to the right place.




ROLE DESCRIPTION

The Production Planner is responsible for managing and optimizing production planning, scheduling, and reporting across multiple production lines at our facility in Weirton, WV. The Production Planner ensures alignment across departments and drives collaboration between Operations, Supply Chain, Warehousing and Finance to achieve production goals, efficient resource planning, and costing accuracy.  This role also plays a key part in launching, maintaining, and enhancing Oracle Fusion modules that support manufacturing, inventory, and financial operations.  Relocation assistance is available. 




WHAT YOU'LL DO:

 - Production Planning & Control
   
   - Represent the Production Planning Department at daily operations meetings - communicating any changes or challenges to the current plan.
   
   - Collaborate with Supply Chain, procurement, and warehousing to align on forecast and ensure material availability.
   
   - Create and manage production and trial work orders for multiple lines in Oracle.
   
   - Manage new part cut-over process across multiple production lines.
   
   - Maintain accurate and up-to-date production data within Oracle, including work orders, materials, and resource utilization.
   
   - Work with ERP project teams to define and configure production processes, routings, BOMs, and work centers in Oracle.
   
   - Monitor real-time production progress using dashboards and analytics tools.

 - Oracle Fusion ERP Implementation & Optimization
   
   - Support the implementation and rollout of Oracle Fusion Cloud Manufacturing ensuring seamless integration with operational workflows.
   
   - Work with ERP project teams to define and configure production processes, routings, BOMs, and work centers in Oracle Fusion.
   
   - Participate in User Acceptance Testing (UAT) and system validation for new modules, updates, and enhancements.

 - System Maintenance & Support
   
   - Act as a primary point of contact for production-related ERP issues, troubleshooting data discrepancies and workflow problems.
   
   - Develop and maintain operational dashboards and reports within Oracle and BI tools to support decision-making.
   
   - Partner with IT and Oracle support teams for upgrades, configuration changes, and module enhancements.

 - Collaboration with Finance
   
   - Support Finance in managing standard costing, work order variances, and cost roll-ups within the ERP system.
   
   - Work closely with the Finance Department to ensure accurate cost tracking and reconciliation between production and financial modules in Oracle Fusion
   
   - Ensure accurate recording of material consumption, labor hours, and overhead allocations to maintain integrity of financial data.
   
   - Lead  month-end and year-end closing processes.





WHAT YOU'LL BRING:

 - Bachelor’s degree in Production Management, Supply Chain, Industrial Engineering, Business Systems, or related field.

 - 8+ years of experience in production control, planning, or manufacturing operations.

 - Hands-on experience with Oracle Fusion Cloud ERP, specifically in Manufacturing, Inventory, and Costing modules.

 - Strong understanding of ERP data structures including BOMs, routings, work centers, and cost elements.

 - Familiarity with integration between production and finance modules (General Ledger, Cost Accounting, and Inventory Valuation).

 - Proficient in Oracle reporting tools, analytics dashboards, and Excel.

 - Experience supporting ERP implementation or upgrade projects.

 - Excellent communication and cross-departmental collaboration skills
   


WHERE YOU'LL WORK:


This role is based at Form Factory 1 in Weirton, WV—an easy commute from the city of Pittsburgh, PA. This 550,000-square-foot facility is our hub for high-volume battery production and a leader in the new era of American energy manufacturing. Relocation assistance is available.

Experience with SAP, o9, or comparable enterprise planning and execution platforms.
Experience with Snowflake and modern cloud data architectures.
Experience designing reusable enterprise data products and governed semantic models.

Communicate project status, risks, and recommendations clearly to cross-functional partners and management
Provide data-driven supplier health updates and recommendations with minimal supervision
Perform other related duties as assigned
Education & Experience
Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Biomedical Engineering, or equivalent experience (advanced degree preferred)
Minimum 2 years of experience in supplier engineering, manufacturing engineering, or quality engineering
Hands-on experience with MIM, machined metal, or plastic injection molded preferred
Experience supporting high-volume manufacturing environments, preferably in medical devices or regulated industries

Proficiency in Microsoft Excel, Word, and Project
Experience with ERP systems such as SAP or Agile preferred
Experience with Minitab or statistical analysis software is a plus
CAD / 3D modeling experience is a plus

Ability to travel domestically and internationally as needed (approximately 25%)
Must be able to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced manufacturing environment

The DaVinci Specialist is a dedicated program execution & clinical education partner for hospitals running a da Vinci robotic surgery program.   Based on its expertise, this role focuses on identifies and tailors the nature and extent of staff in-servicing, day-to-day program execution, technology onboarding and operational support, communicating identified needs to hospital OR operations and leadership. Partner with the local CSR/CSM and cross-functional business partners to create, own, scale and execute best practices and deployment of ecosystem resources.

Support adoption of digital solutions by helping customers build comfort and capability through in-servicing and troubleshooting.

Job Description:
Change Lead, Digital Transformation Reinvention
Digital Transformation Reinvention (DTR) is a strategic enterprise-wide transformation that brings together Digital Foundations, Value Creation, Digital Products, Data & AI, DT Talent, and Digital Upskilling to enable new ways of working and accelerate business outcomes. As Change Lead, you will play a pivotal role in ensuring leaders, managers, and associates are prepared, enabled, and supported to successfully adopt and sustain the changes required to deliver transformation results.
This is a highly influential, hands-on leadership role focused on enterprise organizational change rather than program management, communications delivery, or workstream ownership. The successful candidate will translate complex and often ambiguous transformation initiatives into a clear change architecture, targeted interventions, and measurable adoption outcomes. Working closely with senior leaders and cross-functional stakeholders, you will drive readiness, sponsorship, behavior change, and adoption across a large-scale global transformation, ensuring benefits are realized and sustained over time.
What Are We Looking For?
Bachelor's degree in Business, Organizational Development, Human Resources, Psychology, Change Management, or a related discipline, or equivalent professional experience. Relevant change management certification preferred.
8+ years of progressive experience leading enterprise-wide digital, technology, operating model, workforce, or business transformation initiatives within complex global organizations.
Deep expertise in organizational change management, including readiness assessment, stakeholder engagement, adoption, behavior change, and sustainment.
Proven success developing and executing enterprise change strategies, sponsorship models, impact assessments, adoption frameworks, and intervention plans that drive measurable business outcomes.
Strong ability to assess organizational impacts across people, processes, technology, governance, roles, skills, capabilities, and ways of working, while proactively identifying readiness risks, resistance points, and adoption barriers.
Demonstrated ability to influence, coach, and constructively challenge senior leaders, helping them effectively sponsor and lead teams through change in ambiguous and evolving environments.
Experience designing and implementing targeted interventions that accelerate stakeholder understanding, commitment, adoption, and advocacy.
Exceptional analytical, facilitation, stakeholder management, problem-solving, and decision-making capabilities, with the ability to translate complex transformation requirements into actionable change strategies.
Experience establishing adoption metrics, readiness measures, dashboards, and feedback mechanisms to monitor progress, evaluate effectiveness, and drive continuous improvement.
Proven ability to work effectively within global matrix organizations, coordinating enterprise-wide initiatives while enabling local market or segment activation.
Strong judgment and professionalism when handling sensitive, confidential, or incomplete information.
Experience supporting transformations involving digital products, data and AI, technology modernization, enterprise capability building, workforce upskilling, and/or federated global organizations preferred.
What Will Be Your Key Responsibilities?
Lead Enterprise Change Strategy & Transformation Adoption
Define and lead the enterprise change strategy and implementation roadmap for Digital Transformation Reinvention (DTR).
Develop and maintain an integrated change architecture that links transformation objectives to impacted audiences, required behavior shifts, readiness risks, interventions, and adoption measures.
Translate transformation priorities into clear people, capability, leadership, and behavior requirements.
Establish change management standards, governance, methodologies, and best practices across transformation workstreams.
Integrate change, readiness, and adoption milestones into the overall transformation roadmap.
Assess Organizational Impact & Drive Readiness
Lead enterprise-wide assessments across people, processes, technology, governance, roles, skills, and ways of working.
Maintain a comprehensive view of stakeholder impacts, organizational readiness, and adoption risks across the transformation portfolio.
Identify resistance points, adoption barriers, and critical dependencies, implementing mitigation plans to address risks proactively.
Ensure impact assessments and readiness plans evolve as transformation priorities, scope, or design decisions change.
Enable Leaders, Managers & Sponsors to Drive Change
Define and activate a sponsorship model that promotes visible leadership ownership of transformation outcomes.
Coach and equip senior leaders and managers to confidently lead teams through ambiguity, change, and transition.
Design and implement interventions that move key stakeholder groups from awareness and understanding to adoption, advocacy, and sustained behavior change.
Partner with leaders to reinforce the actions and behaviors necessary for successful transformation adoption.
Partner Across Workstreams & Segments
Collaborate with transformation workstream leaders to embed change management into solution design and delivery.
Coordinate with segment and market counterparts to validate impacts, assess readiness, and support local activation efforts.
Maintain a unified enterprise approach to stakeholder engagement, communication, and leadership action.
Surface cross-functional and cross-segment adoption risks, dependencies, and challenges for leadership decision-making and escalation.
Measure Adoption & Sustain Transformation Outcomes
Define and track leading and lagging indicators that measure readiness, adoption, behavior change, and business value realization.
Establish readiness baselines and maintain enterprise adoption dashboards that provide actionable insights.
Monitor adoption progress, evaluate intervention effectiveness, and recommend course corrections when needed.
Create feedback loops that translate stakeholder insights into meaningful improvements and sustainable business outcomes.
Partner with Change Communications & Key Stakeholders
Work closely with the Change Communications Lead to align change and communications strategies through a single integrated roadmap.
Provide readiness, stakeholder, and adoption insights that inform communication priorities, audience engagement, and sequencing.
Ensure communications reinforce required leadership actions and behavior changes, not just awareness.
Build strong partnerships with transformation leaders, People & Organization teams, segment stakeholders, and enabling functions to support lasting transformation success.

Segment: Mars Petcare (Greenies)

Shift: Night Shift (6:00 PM – 6:30 AM) on a 2-2-3 Rotating Schedule (Alternating weekends off)
Job Type: Full-Time, Permanent
Join Our Greenies Team in North Kansas City
At Mars Petcare, we are passionate about pets. Our Greenies brand is dedicated to keeping pets healthy and happy, and we manufacture our world-renowned products right here in our highly desirable, fully climate-controlled North Kansas City facility.
Being a Mars Associate is all about opportunity. The opportunity to do the kind of challenging, interesting work that shapes the world’s best-loved brands. To work with real purpose, supported by talented, friendly people from all sorts of different backgrounds.
Whether you are an experienced warehouse professional, a skilled forklift operator looking for a stable day-shift position, or a transitioning military Veteran, Reservist, or National Guard member, we welcome your unique talents! We highly value the dedication, safety-first mindset, and structured teamwork developed in the military and look forward to helping you build a successful civilian career.
Job Summary
The Material Handler is responsible for the end-to-end logistics flow within our plant. This dual-focus role handles all incoming packaging and raw ingredients, manages safe product movement inside the site, loads outbound trailers for shipment, completes all logistics paperwork, and maintains perfect inventory control. This associate works closely with production, purchasing, receiving, shipping, and quality teams to ensure seamless plant operations in a clean, temperature-controlled environment.
Key Responsibilities
Receiving & Inbound Logistics
Receive and verify all incoming raw materials, ingredients, packaging, and components against purchase orders and shipping manifests.
Use a forklift to safely unload inbound trucks and transfer materials to their correct designated storage locations.
Conduct strict quality and food safety checks on incoming materials, including collecting product samples and verifying supplier paperwork.
Collaborate with external logistics departments and freight carriers to ensure correct and safe delivery of production materials.
Material Handling & Warehouse Operations
Safely and accurately operate material handling equipment (including forklifts) to transport inventory, raw materials, WIP (work-in-process), and finished goods throughout the facility.
Support production schedules by ensuring that the correct materials are issued and staged in production areas when needed.
Stage, build, and load outbound trailers for shipment, ensuring proper cargo weight distribution and trailer utilization.
Ensure proper labeling, sorting, FIFO (First-In, First-Out) rotation, and general organization of all materials in storage areas.
Inventory, Systems, & Documentation
Scan and track material movements using warehouse management systems to ensure perfect real-time inventory accountability.
Perform daily cycle counts, participate in precision monthly inventories, and assist with formal physical audits.
Investigate inventory discrepancies promptly and report findings to management.
Generate, review, and complete accurate shipping/receiving paperwork, logging all transactions accurately into the plant database.
Safety, Quality, & Food Safety Culture
Participate and adhere to all food safety requirements, Quality Management Processes (QMPs), and site safety programs, championing a safety-first culture.
Maintain a clean, organized, and sanitary warehouse environment in accordance with Good Manufacturing Practices (GMPs).
Promptly report any safety, food safety, or quality concerns to leadership.
Position Requirements
Minimum Qualifications:
Education: High school diploma, GED, or equivalent civilian/military education.
Experience: Proven experience in warehouse logistics, receiving, shipping, or material handling roles.
Equipment: Demonstrated experience operating a forklift safely in an industrial or warehouse environment.
Physical Ability: Must be in good physical condition with the ability to stand and walk for extended periods, bend, reach, climb, and safely lift up to 40 pounds manually.
Technical Literacy: Working knowledge of basic computer programs for entering data, record keeping, and maintaining inventory logs.
Core Skills: Basic math skills, a keen eye for detail, strong organizational skills, and excellent written and verbal communication abilities.
Teamwork: Demonstrated ability to work in a high-performing team environment with a willingness to learn and be coached.
Military & Veteran Technical Equivalency Guide
At Mars, we recognize that your military service has prepared you to excel in logistical operations. Your training in high-stakes material movement, precision inventory tracking, and supply chain management maps directly to this role. If you served in any of the following specialties, we highly encourage you to apply:
U.S. Army: Automated Logistical Specialist (92A), Unit Supply Specialist (92Y), Cargo Specialist (88H), Motor Transport Operator (88M), Ammunition Specialist (89B). Your experience with warehouse databases, material handling equipment (MHE), and precise property book audits is an excellent fit.
U.S. Navy: Logistics Specialist (LS), Storekeeper, Aviation Storekeeper (AK). Your experience managing inventory, shipboard supply warehouses, and processing shipping manifests maps directly to our material tracking systems.
U.S. Air Force: Materiel Management (2S0X1), Traffic Management (2T0X1), Ground Transportation (2T1X1). Your training in cargo loading, receiving inspections, strict compliance with safety procedures, and inventory precision is an exact match.
U.S. Marine Corps: Warehouse Clerk (3051), Supply Administration & Operations (3043), Logistics/Embarkation Specialist (0431), Motor Vehicle Operator (3531). Your focus on cargo staging, load planning, and material handling equipment matches our shipping and receiving operations.
U.S. Coast Guard: Storekeeper (SK), Marine Science Technician.
What We Offer (Total Rewards & Benefits)
At Mars, being an associate is more than a job—it's an opportunity to build a long-term career. We provide a competitive, industry-leading package starting on your very first day:
Compensation: Competitive base pay based on experience, shift differentials, and significant overtime (OT) potential.
Annual Bonus: Eligibility for our annual performance-based company bonus and annual merit increases.
Health & Wellness: Comprehensive Medical, Vision, and Dental insurance starting on Day One.
Retirement Planning: An exceptional 401(k) program with up to 6% company match.
Work-Life Balance: Generous paid vacation time, paid holidays, and predictable rotating 2-2-3 day shifts.
Family Support: Paid Parental Leave, plus Short-Term and Long-Term Disability.
Career Growth: Access to top-tier learning and development through Mars University.
Onsite Perks: Access to our onsite gym.
About Mars, Incorporated
Mars is a family-owned business with over a century of history making diverse products and offering services for people and the pets people love. We produce some of the world’s best-loved brands: M&M’s®, SNICKERS®, TWIX®, MILKY WAY®, DOVE®, PEDIGREE®, ROYAL CANIN®, WHISKAS®, EXTRA®, ORBIT®, 5™, SKITTLES®, BEN’S ORIGINAL®, and COCOAVIA®.
Alongside our consumer brands, we proudly take care of half of the world’s pets through our nutrition, health, and services businesses such as Banfield Pet Hospitals™, BluePearl®, Linnaeus, AniCura, VCA™, and Pet Partners™.
The Mars Five Principles – Quality, Responsibility, Mutuality, Efficiency, and Freedom – inspire our 130,000 Associates to take action every day toward creating the world we want tomorrow.

title: Cloud Principal Hardware Engineer
location: United States, California, Aliso Viejo; United States, Washington, Redmond; United States, California, Mountain View
description:
Overview
Microsoft Silicon, Cloud Hardware, and Infrastructure Engineering (SCHIE) is the team behind Microsoft’s expanding Cloud Infrastructure and responsible for powering Microsoft’s “Intelligent Cloud” mission. SCHIE delivers the core infrastructure and foundational technologies for Microsoft’s over 200 online businesses including Bing, MSN, Office 365, Xbox Live, Teams, OneDrive, and the Microsoft Azure platform globally with our server and data center infrastructure, security and compliance, operations, globalization, and manageability solutions. Our focus is on smart growth, high efficiency, and delivering a trusted experience to customers and partners worldwide and we are looking for passionate engineers to help achieve that mission.
As Microsoft’s cloud business continues to grow, the ability to deploy new offerings and HW infrastructure on time, in high volume, with high quality and lowest cost is of paramount importance. To achieve this goal, the SCHIE team is instrumental in defining and delivering measures of success for hardware design, qualification, fleet support, scale, and sustainability related to Microsoft cloud hardware.
Azure Memory and Storage Center of Excellence (AMS CoE) is part of the SCHIE organization focusing on memory and storage devices going into the cloud hardware servers. AMS provides memory and storage solutions to Azure and drives memory and storage suppliers to deliver high quality products that meet our requirements. AMS CoE also leads Azure Fault Prediction and Detection (AFPD), the platform that predicts, detects and repairs hardware failures across the Azure fleet.
We are looking for a Cloud Principal Hardware Engineer to scale AFPD across hardware components in the Azure fleet and to lead hands-on hardware resiliency for the platform.
The opportunity:
Every hour a server sits unhealthy is an hour of lost customer capacity. AFPD turns hardware, firmware and OS telemetry into early detection and prediction of failures, moves customer workloads off failing nodes, and sends a targeted repair for the part that failed. Repair outcomes and supplier failure analysis then improve the next rule or model.
You will be working on incorporating into the platform components such as storage, memory, power supply, CPU, GPU, NIC, HBA/FPGA, cables and the rest of the server, and you will be the subject matter expert the team relies on when a failure needs to be prevented. Across millions of nodes, each improvement means fewer VM interruptions for customers and faster return of online capacity.
Why this role:
Your impact shows up in fleet availability and customer uptime, quarter over quarter. You will set the hardware direction for a platform that influences production infrastructure at a scale, and you will work directly with Azure engineering, component teams and leading hardware suppliers.
#SCHIE #azurehwjobs
Responsibilities
Lead failure analysis across server components: characterize failure modes from fleet telemetry and logs and confirm root cause with repair results and supplier failure analysis.
Define the signals, thresholds, targeted diagnostics and repair recipes, and work with component teams for the root cause analysis.
Improve isolation accuracy so each repair address the source of failures: improve efficacy of the detection and repair services.
Partner with software engineers and data scientists on detection rules and prediction models; set precision targets and validation gates before a rule or model takes action on production nodes.
Use AI agents and machine learning to automate failure analysis, live-site triage and supplier RCA follow-up, and to shorten the time from a new failure signature to a detection rule.
Lead root cause and corrective actions with server components, including firmware fixes, and feed the learnings back into the platform.
Lead as the senior hardware escalation point for live-site incidents, from triage through root cause to fleet-wide mitigation.
Make new server generations and AI/GPU platforms platform-ready before they reach production, with detection, isolation and repair coverage at launch.
Track and improve metrics & mentor engineers across the team.
Qualifications
Required Qualifications
Bachelor's Degree in Computer Science or related technical field AND 6+ years technical engineering experience with coding in languages including, but not limited to, C, C++, C#, Java, JavaScript, or Python OR equivalent experience.
Other Requirements:
Ability to meet Microsoft, customer and/or government security screening requirements are required for this role. These requirements include but are not limited to the following specialized security screenings:
Microsoft Cloud Background Check: This position will be required to pass the Microsoft Cloud Background Check upon hire/transfer and every two years thereafter.
Preferred Quilifications:
Master’s Degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or related field AND 7+ years technical engineering experience
